tasks.title: E09 in full from its design
tasks.brief: You are the only coder on epic E09 (Reports and specialist findings). Implement it in full from its product brief docs/product/tdd/E09.md and docs/SYSTEM.md (its module, ports and seams; this epic has no design): every section, and every R, V and D of its acceptance matrix with a test, including end to end tests on the real stack. docs/build/E09/PLAN.md and ticket_tasks in docs/build/E09/tasks.json describe one split of this work with briefs, tests and gates: use them as a guide and checklist; the design and docs/SYSTEM.md win where they differ. Build in this order: domain, application, adapters, api, user interface, and run your tests as you go. If an epic you depend on has no code yet, code against its port protocol and the kernel fakes (docs/SYSTEM.md section 10).

ticket_tasks.title: Report domain policy and private lifecycle application workflows
ticket_tasks.brief:
Read AGENTS.md, docs/SYSTEM.md and docs/requests/COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md Part A first, followed by every reads entry. This is a standalone brief for E09, all E09-01/02/03 work retained. There is no docs/tdd/E09.md, docs/requests/E09.md or E09 design review at planning time. Implement from docs/product/tdd/E09.md sections Product contract and Required work and acceptance, SYSTEM and the binding decisions. Do not write/edit a design. Only owned_paths are writable, including tests. These directories instantiate the reports module/layer/test/feature templates in SYSTEM 4.1/4.2/4.3/6.1 (docs/SYSTEM.md:74, :100, :137, :1625). Recheck repository existence and every docs/build/*/tasks.json before writing. No git, engine edits, shared configuration edits or provider copies. English only, with no em/en dash or spaced hyphen used as a dash.

Use SYSTEM 5.1 IdFactory/require_id, 5.2 Clock and corrected observed time, 5.3 MissionClock where mission boundaries matter, 5.4 Decimal Quantity/Unit/UnitRegistry and approved WireUnitConverter, 5.5 ProblemError/StorageUnavailable and the shared ErrorEnvelope mapper, 5.6 immutable ReleaseHandle/ConfigReader/ConfigReleaseReader and atomic loader validation, 5.7 UnitOfWork/ReadSnapshot/StorageSession and mandatory Audience/replication declarations, 5.8 CommandIdentity/IdempotencyStore/ResultVisibility/CommandIntents and mission-life receipts, 5.8.1 PrivateIntent/SealedPrivateRef/PrivateReceipt/PrivateRecordCoordinator/PrivateReferenceWriter/PrivateKeyVault, 5.9 complete AuditEntry, 5.10 health/scheduler and 5.10.1 TaskQueue/TaskRunner/TaskRegistration, 5.11 HubSettings/SettingSpec, 5.12 ModuleRegistry. Never implement shared transactions, deduplication, retries, migrations, clock correction, encryption, backup or recovery infrastructure. SYSTEM 6.2 requires uv run --project hub; 6.4 requires generated module import contracts; 6.5 requires generated effective models with unchanged guarded base contracts. Sections 7.1/7.2/7.4, 8.3/8.6, 9 and 10 govern retention, private deletion, current object/field/purpose grants, durable capture and hard dependencies E01/E02/E05. Use exact provider protocols and kernel.testing when providers are unbuilt; no invented replacement shared types/fakes. Acceptance uses the real providers.

Apply PLAN Design decisions and Design deviations. P1 to P7 are coordinator requests, not approved interfaces. The canonical request file cannot be created in this planner's edit scope. A missing signature/shape/setting blocks its dependent work until the coordinator files and settles it. Do independent authorized work, preserve each blocked acceptance obligation and report it. Never ship a proposed endpoint, schema extension, configuration document, source-span convention, private reader or ReportQueries signature. No skip, xfail, placeholder, production test branch or empty test collection closes an obligation.

All bytes, names, source hashes, private metadata, extraction drafts and spans are encrypted private-store content under D18. Hub metadata and generic tasks contain only opaque references, keyed fingerprints and safe codes; private text never goes to audit, errors, logs, prompts, global indexes, sync or browser persistence. Only human-confirmed validated fields cross to clinical records. Officer/helper/station roles alone grant no report access. An assistant cannot confirm or change safety state. No default patient, origin, time, unit, value or normal result. Preserve LIVE/REPLAY/SIM, original quantities and disagreements. Unknown dates remain null/date-only until an approved time mapping exists. Content comes from validated configuration/backend state, never literals or example fallbacks. Copy generated field names, enums and nullability exactly.

Tests first, with source-checked expected results and R/V/D/invariant IDs in collected test names or the agreed trace registration. Hypothesis/fast-check cover every parser/rule and finite, zero, negative, empty, maximum, null and incompatible-unit boundaries. Inputs live only in explicit-profile fixtures/eval; examples are illustrative source material. Unit/integration tests have injected clocks/IDs, no network or real devices. T5 owns real-stack acceptance; it cannot use in-hub mocks. Applicable AGENTS 6 failures include crashes at every command boundary, duplicate/late retries and wrong targets, concurrent clients, clock jumps/mission boundaries, full disk, corrupt/missing config, incomplete/disagreeing readings, absent/incapacitated owner, long ground outage and cross-crew privacy. Failures never look accepted or safe. Named bounds come only from SYSTEM 5.11 and approved module descriptors, never arbitrary literals. Run every assigned gate; after any bug fix rerun the full hub suite. Done requires actual positive/negative evidence, no unresolved assigned acceptance, independent review, CI and coordinator AI-use log attribution. Unbuilt toolchains/providers are blockers, never passing checks. Gate command sources are BUILD-CHARTER 8, SYSTEM 6.2/6.4, E01 15 and E03 15; task paths are substitutions into their documented command templates.

Build the pure policy and use cases, E09-01 immutable metadata, E09-02 confirmation, E09-03 typed specialist validation. Leave concrete repositories/parsing to T2, HTTP/registration to T3, screens to T4 and assembled scenarios to T5. SYSTEM 4.2 names reports_report, reports_confirmation and ReportQueries. E01 owns records_observation and ObservationCommands/ObservationReader; E02 supplies ConsentQueries.allows(view, *, subject_person_id: str, recipient: str, scope: tuple[str, str]) -> bool (docs/tdd/E02.md:102), with additional current field/action/purpose projection required by P1. The reports row does not license direct records writes. Publish ReportQueries only after P1 settles exact DTOs/signatures with E12/E15/E16. R-E01-17 is pending, so its proposed accepted-reader signature is not an agreed API. Use internal implementation ports only inside E09 and do not export guessed shared aliases.

Map all Report fields from report.schema.json: report_id, file_sha256, original_name, media_type, bytes, patient_id, nullable author/examination_date/report_date, access_scope's full three-value enum, uploaded_at and extraction_drafts. ExtractionDraft fields are draft_id, source_span {page,start,end}, code, number-or-string value, nullable unit/date, extraction_version and proposed/confirmed/rejected review_status. Keep file_sha256 inside the encrypted document; it may be reconstructed in an authorized wire response, never put into reports_report. ConfirmedFinding's confirmer/time and separate clinician attribution are required by CONTRACTS 2 (docs/product/CONTRACTS.md:30); P2 must supply the missing shared representation. Do not define a second wire finding or encode textual ECG as a numeric Observation/context string. Numeric validation uses approved indicator codes, UCUM mappings and E01 record-quality policy; no clinical threshold invented here.

Upload validates current owner/subject, source and bounded media before PrivateRecordCoordinator.write, then returns only after the shared two-store acknowledgment. Source and each draft publication have immutable version identity/new entry keys. Extract with TaskInput/TaskLease/TaskResult pinned to source, engine and release; generic task input_ref is opaque with keyed input_fingerprint. T2 executes bounded parsing outside the writer. Publish completion through PrivateRecordCoordinator.publish outside any hub UoW; its apply callback returns TaskRunner.complete's boolean exactly. False rejects and rolls back attachment; expired/cancelled/revoked/deleted staging is discarded and keys revoked. TaskHandler.apply cannot confirm a finding. Return null from the registered JobResultProjector when the evidence_ref enum lacks report, as SYSTEM 5.10.1 requires. P4 settles trigger/reconnect identity; no private job payload workaround.

Confirmation uses the shared barrier to verify live source/version/current grant, check P2 revision, patient/date/unit acknowledgment, source coordinates and edited values before one E01 hub UoW appends only confirmed records, reports_confirmation lineage, command result, audit and authorized replication/events. No new public report/observation event exists in CONTRACTS 18. Only decisions confirm/reject and optional value/unit are currently legal in ReportConfirmations (requests.schema.json:896); P2 must settle corrections before implementing them. Same draft twice, repeated IDs in a batch, a changed source or conflicting client must not append two findings. Partial invalid batches produce no accepted subset. Preserve both original and corrected records through append-only lineage; a normal imported value never clears a warning/episode or marks a measurement gap addressed without the owning module's valid evidence path.

Deletion uses PrivateRecordCoordinator.delete/CommandIntents and SYSTEM 7.4, not local key erasure. Deny reads/leases and cancel generations before all-version revocation, then tombstone; pending revocation is retryable INTERNAL_ERROR for endpoints lacking a pending shape, never accepted deletion. Retain append-only confirmed clinical records with deleted-source attribution. P4 must settle the public route before wiring. Sharing uses P5's approved immutable recipient snapshot, never recipient vault decryption. Fail closed while the owner is absent; fixed help remains independent.

Write tests first: T-E09-01 (R14, D18) immutable fields/nulls/origins and explicit owner checks; T-E09-02 (R14/R16,V21,V15) patient/date/unit/span confirmation validation and no accepted draft; T-E09-03 (E09-03,V38) all five specialist families, numeric/text/date/interpretation attribution after P2/P3; T-E09-04 (AGENTS durability/privacy) identity bound to operation/target/body/parameters, revoked replay and atomic duplicate/concurrent confirmation; T-E09-05 (D17/D18) task pinning, boolean completion fence, cancellation/deletion/revocation and explicit unknown output; T-E09-06 (V14,V75) observation-time preservation, configuration-label edit, invalid release retention and existing pins. Property tests verify span/value/unit parsing, duplicate decisions and reject-unconfirmed invariants, with independently checked clinical expectations rather than document-derived assertions. Concrete crash/SQLite evidence belongs to T2/T5, not these fake-port tests. Done when pure rules and workflows plus all listed evidence pass, and agreed protocol exports are usable by T2/T3 without a shared type copy.
gates: uv run --project hub pytest -c hub/pyproject.toml -q hub/tests/reports/domain hub/tests/reports/application
uv run --project hub ruff check hub/src/crew_health/reports/domain hub/src/crew_health/reports/application hub/tests/reports/domain hub/tests/reports/application
uv run --project hub ruff format --check hub/src/crew_health/reports/domain hub/src/crew_health/reports/application hub/tests/reports/domain hub/tests/reports/application
uv run --project hub mypy --strict --config-file hub/pyproject.toml hub/src/crew_health/reports/domain hub/src/crew_health/reports/application hub/tests/reports/domain hub/tests/reports/application
uv run --project hub python -m crew_health.app.import_contracts --output /tmp/crew-health-e09-T1-imports.ini
uv run --project hub lint-imports --config /tmp/crew-health-e09-T1-imports.ini

Use SYSTEM 5.7 StorageSession typed SQL with bounded rows/statements and the E01 migration registry discovered through module.py. Implement the E09 PrivateReferenceWriter.attach/tombstone adapters exactly SYSTEM 5.8.1. attach transient plaintext only for validation, never hub persistence; each repository mutation declares the reference-only local replication change with export_projection None, SYSTEM 5.7/5.7.1. Accepted clinical projections belong to records, approved sharing to P5; no raw report replication. Private receipts and backup lock order remain barrier, private seal, hub write, private receipt. Coordinate paired private schema migrations with E01; create only the agreed E09 ciphertext tables, never modify another private writer's tables or shared recovery schema. Follow approved P4 quarantine semantics: bounded encrypted retention, safe reason code, no inline active document, no fallback draft. P6 must settle cross-platform parser containment, dependencies, resource caps and source-coordinate meaning before invoking untrusted content. Never add a network parser, a new top-level worker package or unapproved shell command. A sandbox launcher is a provider interface, not a subprocess convenience to invent.

The TaskHandler executes deterministic bounded text extraction into proposed fields outside hub write transactions, under current owner authority, with immutable source/engine/release pins and generation identity. Actual source interpretation needs schema/registry validation in T1. PDF embedded instructions, scripts, embedded files, links and paths remain inert; no eval/exec, document-driven imports, filesystem traversal, external-resource fetch or model tool invocation. Image-only/unsupported extraction means explicit unavailability; human source review/manual entry is the independent path. No OCR/image diagnosis or fabricated normal values. Use SYSTEM 5.11 private/report/task/storage/worker caps and P6's approved page/pixel/text/span descriptors. P6 supplies engine/dependency versions and provenance; do not invent identifiers/default budgets. T1 owns coordinated publish; adapters stage encrypted outputs, discard unreferenced results and use shared vault revocation rather than deleting accepted versions to meet a cap.

Write first: T-E09-07 (R14,AGENTS durability) real temporary SQLite and real private coordinator/vault fault matrix at private commit, hub reference commit, marker and ACK; retry after each yields no accepted loss/duplicate; distinguish unreferenced orphan disposal from accepted ciphertext repair. T-E09-08 (R14/privacy) inspect hub tables/generic tasks/logs for canaries, filenames and guessable file hash; preserve bytes in owner-authorized round-trip. T-E09-09 (V22,AGENTS parser bounds) property/adversarial cases for MIME mismatch, empty/maximum/over-limit bytes, corrupt/decompression-heavy input, pages/pixels/text/span caps, Unicode coordinates and injection content; prove contained timeouts and cancellation leave no clinical writes. Create bounded valid, corrupt and malicious test files plus their explicit-profile manifest only in the owned eval/scenarios/E09/inputs/ directory. No clinical seed data in source/tests. This input directory is T2-owned and ready before T5 starts, so there is no dependency on a downstream test author. T5 consumes it read-only. T-E09-10 (D18,AGENTS privacy/durability) concurrent upload/extraction/deletion with paired backup, source/confirm race, interrupted revoke, old backup of A/B after A deletion, retained B readable and A irrecoverable with current vault. T-E09-11 (AGENTS failures) disk full/locked/I/O/corrupt ciphertext are typed failures with no false success; real restart recovers correctly; incomplete metadata stays unknown. Use documented E01/E20 fault controls, no production test switch. Startup missing/corrupt config retains last good or safe mode, never bypasses validation. Clock corrections cannot refresh source age or revive a task generation.

Done when actual adapters implement T1 contracts, migration/strict typing/import gates pass and all private-store/parser fault cases have evidence. A provider fake cannot certify vault durability, sandbox security or backup. Missing P1/P4/P6 controls stay explicit blockers for their tests; report them rather than replacing them.

After the cache window, only the authorized matching closed accepted_command receipt counts; different target/body/parameters return DUPLICATE_COMMAND with null current_state. Never leak a report ID or source fields in an unauthorized error. Map typed errors using SYSTEM 5.5/D5; declared 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, 415 UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE, 422 INVALID_VALUE/REPORT_UNCONFIRMED, 428 VERSION_REQUIRED and 409 STALE_VERSION remain tested at their declared operations. module.py registers T1/T2 factories with explicit provide.requires, routers, ReportQueries after P1, exact private-record writer record kinds, task handler/version/result projector/public_kind report_extraction, local current-grant task audiences, approved settings descriptors, ID prefixes and necessary startup callbacks. It performs no I/O on import/register and never instantiates a second coordinator, queue or vault. Pin staged inputs/results; wire the boolean publication callback through T1, no nested transaction. Existing confirmed observations are records' responsibility. E09 has no public report events or direct warning/measurement mutations. Missing optional parser/model/ground only degrades its own capability; missing required config/authorization/storage keeps the affected operation unavailable. Never implement shared transactions, deduplication, retries, migrations, clock correction, encryption, backup or recovery infrastructure. SYSTEM 6.2 requires uv run --project hub; 6.4 requires generated module import contracts; 6.5 requires generated effective models with unchanged guarded base contracts. Use exact provider protocols and kernel.testing when providers are unbuilt; no invented replacement shared types/fakes. Acceptance uses the real providers.

Apply PLAN Design decisions and Design deviations. P1 to P7 are coordinator requests, not approved interfaces. The canonical request file cannot be created in this planner's edit scope. A missing signature/shape/setting blocks its dependent work until the coordinator files and settles it. Do independent authorized work, preserve each blocked acceptance obligation and report it. Never ship a proposed endpoint, schema extension, configuration document, source-span convention, private reader or ReportQueries signature. No skip, xfail, placeholder, production test branch or empty test collection closes an obligation.

All bytes, names, source hashes, private metadata, extraction drafts and spans are encrypted private-store content under D18. Hub metadata and generic tasks contain only opaque references, keyed fingerprints and safe codes; private text never goes to audit, errors, logs, prompts, global indexes, sync or browser persistence. Only human-confirmed validated fields cross to clinical records. Officer/helper/station roles alone grant no report access. An assistant cannot confirm or change safety state. No default patient, origin, time, unit, value or normal result. Preserve LIVE/REPLAY/SIM, original quantities and disagreements. Unknown dates remain null/date-only until an approved time mapping exists. Content comes from validated configuration/backend state, never literals or example fallbacks. Copy generated field names, enums and nullability exactly.

Tests first, with source-checked expected results and R/V/D/invariant IDs in collected test names or the agreed trace registration. Hypothesis/fast-check cover every parser/rule and finite, zero, negative, empty, maximum, null and incompatible-unit boundaries. Inputs live only in explicit-profile fixtures/eval; examples are illustrative source material. Unit/integration tests have injected clocks/IDs, no network or real devices. T5 owns real-stack acceptance; it cannot use in-hub mocks. Applicable AGENTS 6 failures include crashes at every command boundary, duplicate/late retries and wrong targets, concurrent clients, clock jumps/mission boundaries, full disk, corrupt/missing config, incomplete/disagreeing readings, absent/incapacitated owner, long ground outage and cross-crew privacy. Failures never look accepted or safe. Named bounds come only from SYSTEM 5.11 and approved module descriptors, never arbitrary literals. Run every assigned gate; after any bug fix rerun the full hub suite. Done requires actual positive/negative evidence, no unresolved assigned acceptance, independent review, CI and coordinator AI-use log attribution. Unbuilt toolchains/providers are blockers, never passing checks. Gate command sources are BUILD-CHARTER 8, SYSTEM 6.2/6.4, E01 15 and E03 15; task paths are substitutions into their documented command templates.

Build only the crew reports feature and its component/property tests, E09-01 upload/status/source metadata, E09-02 side-by-side review and E09-03 specialist structured entry. Leave backend to T1/T2/T3, generic shell/session/offline machinery to E03/E02/E20, RecordsView to E15, measurement gaps to E05 and real-stack browser acceptance to T5. This task can build components in parallel with backend work after its contracts land; HTTP-dependent validation waits for T3, not a mock claiming real acceptance. Python ruff/mypy/import-linter do not apply to this TS-only task; its pnpm lint/strict typecheck/unit/property gates are the matching obligations.

Use Vue 3/TypeScript strict and only @crew-health/contracts generated types/client (SYSTEM 6.3). Implement fields from Report and ReportConfirmations exactly, preserving all nulls and number/string draft values. Current operations are uploadReport/getReport/confirmExtraction at docs/product/api/openapi.yaml:5037/:5149/:5219; never hardcode a new route, request property, extraction Job identifier convention, revision counter or upload origin. P2/P4 must supply revision/identity/date correction, source-content viewing, extraction status/cancel linkage and manual findings APIs before those controls can submit. Source next to draft is required, so metadata-only UI does not complete review. Use an inert/sandboxed source viewer under P4/P6, never execute PDF/image content, follow embedded links, expose filesystem paths or render extracted HTML. Keep malicious document instructions as quoted content with no actions/tools. Do not claim image interpretation, diagnosis, normal rhythm or personal radiation dose from unrelated inputs.

Review requires deliberate patient identity, examination/report/finding date, original/proposed value, unit, source span and interpretation-origin checks, followed by explicit per-field confirm/reject. The confirmation button never fires automatically on upload/job completion. Separate technical acceptance from clinician diagnosis and attribute source author, confirmer/time and clinician interpretation. Keep proposed, rejected, missing, uncertain, corrupt, quarantined and unavailable states distinct; do not infer acceptance from a 409 error code without SYSTEM 5.8's complete matching receipt. Two-browser stale revision requires refresh/review, not automatic overwrite. Date-only values stay dates; no JavaScript Date conversion to fabricated midnight.

Implement the five configured form families eye, ECG, laboratory, imaging and dosimetry from input-dictionary.csv:89/:95 onwards and the approved P3 definitions, including eye/method/laterality where applicable, instrument/source/date/interpretation, laboratory units/reference intervals and dosimeter quantity/exposure interval/location. Form codes, captions, labels, units, placeholders, validation words and accessibility copy come from approved ui-copy.json/indicator-catalog.json/unit-mapping.json or authorized backend data. No E09 task edits these E03/E01-owned documents. Existing vital-sign catalog examples do not supply the specialist definitions; P3 is a prerequisite, not permission to type clinical content into .vue/.ts. A scratch non-safety label change must change the rendered feature without code change.

Join E03's agreed feature registration and session lifecycle interfaces under P7; do not edit shell/router/slots/package.json or invent a second sessionEpoch/subscription/reset API. On lock, sign-out, grant loss, route leave or session epoch change, abort work, release source URLs and clear report/draft DOM and memory before another person can render. Fence late fetch/task responses by the current session. No source bytes, metadata, drafts, confirmations, filenames, hashes or private report responses in IndexedDB, localStorage, Cache API, service-worker cache or durable command queues. P3 private content is never persisted even encrypted by the generic queue. Hub loss leaves a visibly unsaved in-memory edit only; lock clears it. Reconnect through the approved existing task identity and fetch current authorized state, never duplicate extraction.

Write component tests first: T-E09-16 (R14/V21) side-by-side source review, explicit patient/date/unit confirmation, per-field reject, stale revision, no automatic acceptance, and malformed receipt rejection using generated examples plus schema-valid boundary cases; these are UI tests, not HTTP acceptance. T-E09-17 (E09-03,V38) each of the five form families, source/clinician attribution and numeric/text/null/date/unit round-trip under approved schemas; no unmeasured defaults. T-E09-18 (AGENTS privacy,V25) lock/sign-out/revocation, old-owner late response, bfcache/resume and route exit clear all private state and object URLs; prove no browser persistence/queue writes. T-E09-19 (R14,V36,V75) keyboard-only labels/errors/statuses, no color-only state, poor/missing extraction with manual fallback, source text treated inert and scratch copy change rendered with no code edit. fast-check covers parser/form boundaries and race sequences. T5 owns tests against the actual running hub for these cases. Done when generated-contract components and property tests pass, real registration/cleanup is wired, all required copy/forms/APIs are approved and T5 can exercise the feature without a UI-specific backend or shared-file edit.
